DSA.description: Data Structures and Algorithms helps you solve programming problems efficiently.

topics.name: Arrays
topics.description: An array is a linear data structure that stores elements in contiguous memory locations.
topics.complexity: Access: O(1), Search: O(n), Insertion: O(n)
keyPoints: Insertion and deletion can be expensive

practice.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element by index in an array?

topics.name: Strings
topics.description: A string is a sequence of characters used to represent text.
keyPoints: Strings are commonly used for text processing
Characters can be accessed using indexes
String operations may create new strings

practice.question: Which data type is commonly used to store text?

topics.name: Linked List
topics.description: A linked list is a linear data structure where nodes are connected using references.
topics.complexity: Search: O(n), Insertion: O(1) at known position
keyPoints: Each node stores data and a reference
Nodes are not necessarily stored contiguously
Insertion and deletion are efficient at known positions

practice.question: Which part of a linked list node stores the reference to the next node?

topics.name: Stack
topics.description: A stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last In First Out principle.
topics.complexity: Push: O(1), Pop: O(1), Peek: O(1)
keyPoints: Top element can be accessed using Peek

practice.question: Which principle does a stack follow?

topics.name: Queue
topics.description: A queue is a linear data structure that follows the First In First Out principle.

practice.question: Which principle does a queue follow?

topics.name: Recursion
topics.description: Recursion is a technique where a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of a problem.
keyPoints: Useful for tree and divide-and-conquer problems
Can use additional call stack memory

practice.question: What prevents infinite recursion?

topics.name: Binary Search
topics.description: Binary Search finds an element in a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search space into two halves.
keyPoints: Search space is divided into halves
Much faster than linear search for large sorted arrays

practice.question: What is required before applying binary search on a normal array?

topics.name: Sorting
topics.description: Sorting algorithms arrange elements in a particular order.
topics.complexity: Depends on algorithm, commonly O(n log n)
keyPoints: Can arrange data ascending or descending
Bubble Sort is simple but slow
Merge Sort uses divide and conquer
Quick Sort is efficient on average

practice.question: Which sorting algorithm commonly has O(n log n) average complexity?

topics.name: Trees
topics.description: A tree is a hierarchical non-linear data structure consisting of nodes connected by edges.

practice.question: Which node is at the top of a tree?

topics.name: Binary Search Tree
topics.description: A Binary Search Tree is a binary tree where smaller values are placed on the left and larger values on the right.
topics.complexity: Average Search: O(log n), Worst: O(n)
keyPoints: Each node has at most two children

practice.question: Which traversal of a BST produces sorted values?

topics.name: Heap
topics.description: A heap is a complete binary tree commonly used to implement priority queues.
topics.complexity: Insert: O(log n), Delete: O(log n), Peek: O(1)
keyPoints: Can be Min Heap or Max Heap
Root contains minimum or maximum element
Used in priority queues and heap sort
topics.example: Max Heap → Root contains maximum value

practice.question: Which element is at the root of a Max Heap?

topics.name: Graph
topics.description: A graph is a non-linear data structure consisting of vertices and edges.
keyPoints: BFS and DFS are common graph traversals

practice.question: Which two components make up a graph?

topics.name: Dynamic Programming
topics.description: Dynamic Programming solves problems by breaking them into overlapping subproblems and storing their results.
topics.example: Fibonacci using DP: dp[n] = dp[n-1] + dp[n-2]

practice.question: What is one important property of problems solved using dynamic programming?

topics.name: Greedy Algorithms
topics.description: Greedy algorithms make the locally optimal choice at each step.
keyPoints: Usually does not reconsider previous choices
Can produce globally optimal solutions for suitable problems
Used in activity selection and Huffman coding

practice.question: What type of choice does a greedy algorithm make?

COA.description: Computer Organization and Architecture explains how computers work internally.

topics.name: Computer Fundamentals
topics.description: Computer fundamentals explain the basic components and working of a computer system.

practice.question: Which component performs most processing operations?

topics.name: Number System
topics.description: Number systems such as binary, decimal, octal and hexadecimal are used in computing.

practice.question: What is the base of the binary number system?

topics.name: Boolean Algebra
topics.description: Boolean algebra is used to represent and simplify logical expressions.

practice.question: Which values are mainly used in Boolean algebra?

topics.name: Logic Gates
topics.description: Logic gates perform basic logical operations in digital circuits.

practice.question: Which gate produces the opposite output?

topics.name: CPU Organization
topics.description: CPU organization explains registers, ALU and control unit operations.

practice.question: Which component performs arithmetic and logical operations?

topics.name: Instruction Cycle
topics.description: The instruction cycle describes how the CPU fetches, decodes and executes instructions.

practice.question: What is the first major step of an instruction cycle?

topics.name: Memory Organization
topics.description: Memory organization explains how different types of memory store data.

practice.question: Which memory is generally faster?

topics.name: Cache Memory
topics.description: Cache memory is a small and fast memory located close to the CPU.
keyPoints: L1 is generally faster than L2 and L3
topics.example: CPU → L1 Cache → L2 Cache → RAM

practice.question: Why is cache memory used?

topics.name: Input Output Organization
topics.description: I/O organization explains how computers communicate with external devices.

practice.question: Which is an input device?

topics.name: Pipeline
topics.description: Instruction pipelining improves CPU performance by overlapping instruction execution stages.
topics.example: Fetch → Decode → Execute → Memory → Write Back

practice.question: What is the main benefit of pipelining?

topics.name: RISC and CISC
topics.description: RISC and CISC are two approaches to processor instruction set design.
keyPoints: RISC often uses fixed instruction formats
CISC can reduce number of instructions per program

practice.question: What does RISC stand for?

topics.name: Control Unit
topics.description: The control unit directs and coordinates operations performed by the CPU.

practice.question: What does the control unit generate?

DBMS.description: Database Management Systems are used to store, organize and retrieve data efficiently.

topics.name: Introduction to DBMS
topics.description: DBMS is software used to create, store, organize and manage databases.

practice.question: What is the main purpose of a DBMS?

topics.name: ER Model
topics.description: The Entity Relationship model represents entities, attributes and relationships in a database.

practice.question: What does ER stand for?

topics.name: Relational Model
topics.description: The relational model organizes data into tables containing rows and columns.

practice.question: What structure is mainly used by the relational model?

topics.name: Keys
topics.description: Database keys identify records and establish relationships between tables.

practice.question: Which key uniquely identifies a record?

topics.name: SQL
topics.description: SQL is used to create, retrieve, modify and manage data in relational databases.

practice.question: Which SQL command retrieves data?

topics.name: Normalization
topics.description: Normalization organizes database tables to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity.
topics.example: Splitting repeated data into separate tables

practice.question: What is a major goal of normalization?

topics.name: Functional Dependency
topics.description: Functional dependency describes relationships between attributes in a relational database.

practice.question: Functional dependencies are mainly used in which DBMS concept?

topics.name: Transactions
topics.description: A transaction is a sequence of database operations treated as one logical unit.

practice.question: Which property ensures that a transaction is all-or-nothing?

topics.name: Concurrency Control
topics.description: Concurrency control manages simultaneous database transactions while maintaining consistency.
topics.example: Two users updating the same record

practice.question: What does concurrency control maintain?

topics.name: Indexing
topics.description: Indexes improve the speed of data retrieval from database tables.

practice.question: What is the main purpose of an index?

topics.name: Database Security
topics.description: Database security protects data from unauthorized access and modification.

practice.question: Which technique helps protect sensitive database data?

topics.name: Joins
topics.description: Joins combine data from multiple tables using related columns.
topics.example: SELECT * FROM students INNER JOIN courses ON students.course_id = courses.id;

practice.question: Which JOIN returns matching rows from both tables?

CN.description: Computer Networks explains how computers communicate and exchange information.

topics.name: Introduction to Networks
topics.description: Computer networks allow devices to communicate and share resources.

practice.question: What is the main purpose of a computer network?

topics.name: OSI Model
topics.description: The OSI model divides network communication into seven layers.
topics.example: Application → Presentation → Session → Transport → Network → Data Link → Physical

practice.question: How many layers are in the OSI model?

topics.name: TCP/IP Model
topics.description: The TCP/IP model is a practical networking model used on the Internet.

practice.question: How many layers are commonly used in the TCP/IP model?

topics.name: Physical Layer
topics.description: The physical layer handles transmission of raw bits over a communication medium.

practice.question: Which OSI layer transmits raw bits?

topics.name: Data Link Layer
topics.description: The data link layer provides node-to-node data transfer and error detection.

practice.question: Which address is mainly associated with the Data Link layer?

topics.name: Network Layer
topics.description: The network layer handles logical addressing and routing of packets.

practice.question: Which device mainly operates at the Network layer?

topics.name: Transport Layer
topics.description: The transport layer provides end-to-end communication between applications.

practice.question: Which protocol provides reliable connection-oriented communication?

topics.name: Application Layer
topics.description: The application layer provides network services directly to applications.

practice.question: Which protocol is commonly used for web communication?

topics.name: IP Addressing
topics.description: IP addressing identifies devices on a network using logical addresses.

practice.question: Which is a valid IPv4 address?

topics.name: Routing
topics.description: Routing determines the best path for packets to travel from source to destination.
topics.example: Source → Router A → Router B → Destination

practice.question: What does routing determine?

topics.name: TCP and UDP
topics.description: TCP provides reliable connection-oriented communication while UDP provides faster connectionless communication.
keyPoints: UDP is commonly used for real-time applications

practice.question: Which protocol is connectionless?

topics.name: DNS
topics.description: DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.

practice.question: What does DNS translate?

topics.name: HTTP and HTTPS
topics.description: HTTP and HTTPS are application layer protocols used for web communication.

practice.question: What does HTTPS provide over HTTP?

OS.description: Operating Systems manage computer hardware, software resources and provide services to applications.

topics.name: Introduction to Operating System
topics.description: An operating system manages hardware resources and provides services to application programs.

practice.question: What is the main role of an operating system?

topics.name: Process Management
topics.description: Process management handles creation, execution and termination of processes.

practice.question: What is a running program called?

topics.name: Process Scheduling
topics.description: Process scheduling determines which process should be executed by the CPU.

practice.question: Which scheduling algorithm uses a time quantum?

topics.name: Threads
topics.description: Threads are lightweight units of execution within a process.

practice.question: Threads belong to which entity?

topics.name: Synchronization
topics.description: Process synchronization coordinates concurrent processes to avoid race conditions.
topics.example: Process A → Critical Section ← Process B

practice.question: Which problem does synchronization help prevent?

topics.name: Deadlock
topics.description: Deadlock occurs when processes wait indefinitely for resources held by each other.
topics.complexity: Depends on detection or avoidance algorithm
topics.example: P1 waits for P2 and P2 waits for P1

practice.question: Which is a necessary condition for deadlock?

topics.name: Memory Management
topics.description: Memory management controls allocation and deallocation of memory to processes.

practice.question: Which OS component manages RAM allocation?

topics.name: Paging
topics.description: Paging divides memory into fixed-size pages and frames.

practice.question: Paging divides logical memory into what?

topics.name: Segmentation
topics.description: Segmentation divides memory into logical segments such as code, data and stack.

practice.question: Segmentation divides memory into what?

topics.name: Virtual Memory
topics.description: Virtual memory allows programs to use more memory than the physically available RAM.

practice.question: Virtual memory mainly uses which storage along with RAM?

topics.name: File System
topics.description: A file system organizes and manages files and directories on storage devices.

practice.question: What does a file system manage?

topics.name: Disk Scheduling
topics.description: Disk scheduling algorithms determine the order in which disk I/O requests are served.

practice.question: Which algorithm is also known as the elevator algorithm?

PYTHON.description: Python is a powerful programming language widely used in software development, data science and artificial intelligence.

topics.name: Python Basics
topics.description: Python basics cover syntax, indentation, variables and fundamental programming concepts.

practice.question: Which function is used to display output in Python?

topics.name: Variables and Data Types
topics.description: Variables store data and Python provides types such as integers, floats, strings and booleans.

practice.question: Which data type stores True or False?

topics.name: Operators
topics.description: Operators perform arithmetic, comparison, logical and other operations.

practice.question: Which operator is used for exponentiation in Python?

topics.name: Conditional Statements
topics.description: Conditional statements execute different blocks depending on whether a condition is true or false.

practice.question: Which keyword is used for a condition in Python?

topics.name: Loops
topics.description: Loops repeatedly execute a block of code.

practice.question: Which loop is commonly used to iterate over a sequence?

topics.name: Functions
topics.description: Functions are reusable blocks of code designed to perform specific tasks.
topics.example: def add(a, b): return a + b

practice.question: Which keyword defines a function in Python?

topics.name: Lists
topics.description: Lists are ordered and mutable collections that can store multiple values.

practice.question: Which property does a Python list have?

topics.name: Tuples
topics.description: Tuples are ordered and immutable collections in Python.

practice.question: Are Python tuples mutable?

topics.name: Sets
topics.description: Sets are unordered collections of unique elements.

practice.question: What does a Python set automatically avoid?

topics.name: Dictionaries
topics.description: Dictionaries store data as key-value pairs.

practice.question: What does a Python dictionary store?

topics.name: Strings
topics.description: Python strings are immutable sequences of Unicode characters.

practice.question: Are Python strings mutable?

topics.name: Object Oriented Programming
topics.description: Object Oriented Programming organizes programs using classes and objects.

practice.question: Which concept allows one class to acquire properties of another?

topics.name: Exception Handling
topics.description: Exception handling allows programs to handle runtime errors safely.

practice.question: Which keyword handles an exception?

topics.name: File Handling
topics.description: File handling allows Python programs to read and write data to files.

practice.question: Which function is used to open a file in Python?

topics.name: Modules and Packages
topics.description: Modules and packages help organize Python code and reuse functionality.

practice.question: Which keyword is used to include a module?
